chunks: And to you be peace, and the mercy of Allah, and His blessings.

And know, along with this, that among most of them there is a grievous narrowness of mind, and ugly avarice, and hoarding of benefits, and domination in sales; and that is a door of harm to the general public, and a defect upon the governors. So prevent them from hoarding, for indeed the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) prevented it.
ai.seo_question: What economic practices did Imam Ali command Malik al-Ashtar to prevent in Egypt?
ai.summary: This directive from Imam Ali’s letter to Malik al-Ashtar highlights the governor’s duty to curb market manipulation, specifically 'ihtikar' (hoarding), which was viewed as a breach of public trust and a sign of moral corruption among officials. By citing the Prophet’s precedent, the Imam establishes economic justice as a core component of Islamic governance, linking the prevention of greed to the protection of the general populace from exploitation.

en.sayed-ali-raza: Know, along with this, that most of them are very narrow-minded, and awfully avaricious. They hoard goods for profiteering and fix high prices for goods. This is a source of harm to the people and a blot on the officers in charge. Stop people from hoarding, because the Messenger of Allāh (S) has prohibited it.
